payload.description: Loop deficiency: a dev session named its story spec <id>.md instead of <id>-<slug>.md (story 21-6). bmad-loop v0.9.1 resolves a spec by the glob <id>-*.md, so it read the finished, committed story as pending, logged a result-less Stop (verdict pending) and armed the stall grace. Closed by hand: git mv to <id>-<slug>.md and a commit. Hole to plug: the studio customization (bmad-build-auto.toml) or the manifest's invoke_dev_with should pin the spec file name, and the pre_commit gate should refuse a stories/ file that does not match <id>-*.md.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor run 20260928-191230-73a0, tasks/21-6-...-dev-1/resultless-stops.jsonl; commit eaf9ea4

payload.description: Loop deficiency: Claude Code 2.1.283 showed the dialog 'Make auto mode your default permission mode?' inside a bmad-loop dev session started with --permission-mode bypassPermissions. The engine's stall nudge was typed into that dialog, which answered it: the sandbox's ~/.claude/settings.json gained permissions.defaultMode=auto at 21:11:02Z and the live session switched to auto mode. The nudge text never reached the agent. Hole to plug: provision-engine.sh should pre-answer the dialog in the sandbox's user settings, and the runbook should name the setting.
payload.evidence: claude-tk-studio-supervisor sandbox, run 20260928-191230-73a0, logs/21-6-...-dev-1.log, 2026-09-28T21:11Z

payload.description: Loop deficiency: an sbx engine reads the Windows host checkout, where files under '* text=auto' are CRLF. TUA's verify gate was red on 2 of 1030 tests (golden .tss compared on LF) in the sandbox and would be on the host; the main PC's WSL clone is LF and hid it. Fixed per project by pinning the format to LF (the-universe-awaits PR #2). Hole to plug: tk-studio onboarding or activate should report text formats a project's tests read byte-exact that are not pinned to LF when the project has an sbx engine.
payload.evidence: claude-the-universe-awaits sandbox, scripts/verify.sh, 2026-09-28; thkennedy/the-universe-awaits#2; thkennedy/tk-studio#84

payload.description: Loop deficiency: story spec files are named <id>-<slug>.md where the id already carries the title slug, so names reach about 150 characters. A clone of the supervisor under a deep folder fails on Windows with 'Filename too long' (MAX_PATH); host verification needs a short-path clone such as «path»<name>. Hole to plug: the task-planning instructions could use short ids (21-6) for file names, or the runbook could set core.longpaths.
payload.evidence: host clone for the 21-5 Windows check, 2026-09-28

payload.description: Loop deficiency: the engine lives only as long as one host-side 'sbx exec' started from a Claude desktop-app session on the agent PC. If that app restarts, the sandbox stops and the engine dies mid-story. Story 22.3 (start.ps1 holds the engine) owns the fix; until then, check the holder process after any app restart on Tim-PC-2.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor Epic 21 launch5, host pid of sbx exec, 2026-09-28

payload.description: Loop deficiency: story 21-5 landed with a race in its signal path (handlers installed after spawn() returned), and its own signal tests passed at its gate by timing. One story later the same tests were red in the engine on every run, the 21-6 review session could not find the cause, consult ruled escalate, and the run paused. Closed by hand: root cause found with timing marks in a scratch copy, fixed in 76ded1b with a test that fails 15 of 15 on the old code. Hole to plug: the verify gate should run process and signal tests more than once (or under a repeat flag) before a story lands, and the consult instructions should name 'run the failing test N times on the baseline and record the failure rate' as the first step on verify-red.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor run 20260928-191230-73a0; commits 92208cf, 76ded1b; PR thkennedy/tk-studio-supervisor#2

payload.description: Loop deficiency: when a run pauses on an escalation after the story's work is committed, the engine's close-out never runs: no studio gate (reconcile), no post_commit meter, no follow-up-review deferral, no squash. Closing story 21-6 by hand took seven steps (commit the pending pass, fix, verify on both hosts, spec status and resolution, reconcile and replan notes, meter from the run dir, trial data and archive). Hole to plug: a studio script or tk-studio-launch verb that closes a landed story by hand in one step, from the runbook's 'when a run pauses' list.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor commits b78a3fa, 6a57518; kb/agent-pc-setup-runbook.md section 3.8

payload.description: Loop deficiency: a headless tk-studio-launch session (epic-22-launch1, Opus 5.5) wrote SPEC.md, met the dirty tree at its second readiness check, and ended by asking the operator for permission to commit. It printed no status block (AD-11: never a question, always the block). The Epic 24 launch committed its own bootstrap; the Epic 20 launch ended blocked. Three launches, three behaviours. Hole to plug: tk-studio-launch should state one rule for its own bootstrap output (commit it on the run branch, then re-check), and conformance should drive the dirty-tree case.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor .bmad-loop/cache/epic-22-launch1/launch.json, 2026-09-28

payload.description: Loop deficiency: story 22-2 landed with a test that fails only on Windows (test/page.test.ts expects '~/planted-home-file'; on win32 the page shows '~\planted-home-file'). The engine's gate runs on Linux only, so it was green. The Windows host run after the story caught it; the product behaviour is right and the fix is one line in the test. Third Windows-only finding after the canonicalPath case fold (21-4) and DW-5. Hole to plug: a Windows leg in the verify gate, for example the supervisor's host tier running 'bun test' in a clone of the story commit before the story is accepted.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor commit 3810a27; host clone run 2026-09-29T00:24Z

payload.description: Loop deficiency: story 22-3 enabled the end-to-end suites on win32 and wrote their win32 paths from Linux, where they cannot run. The first Windows host run failed 29 of 548 tests. Every cause was test-side: .cmd fakes cannot be spawned without a shell (EINVAL), a killed process reports exit code 1 not SIGKILL, bun's folder also holds uv under WinGet, symlinks need a privilege, and the fake sbx used the VM folder as a host folder. Closed by hand in 39596da (no production change); the host is 545 pass, 16 skip, 0 fail. Hole to plug: the same Windows leg as the verify gate needs; a story that touches win32 paths cannot be accepted on a Linux run alone.
payload.evidence: tk-studio-supervisor commits 539dffa, 39596da; «path»

payload.description: Loop deficiency: after 'winget upgrade Docker.sbx' (v0.45.1 to v0.47.0) the daemon was stopped on purpose, and a plain 'sbx ls' issued from a Claude desktop-app session auto-started a new daemon inside the app's container context. That daemon read the sandbox records but could not reach the inner docker engine ('docker daemon is not reachable at «path»'), listed no sandboxes, and every 'sbx exec' failed with 'backend unavailable'. Closed by hand: 'sbx daemon stop', then the 'Docker Sandboxes daemon' logon task (Start-ScheduledTask), which starts it outside the app context. Hole to plug: from a Claude session, run no sbx command but 'sbx daemon status' while the daemon may be down ('sbx ls', 'exec', 'rm' and 'diagnose' all auto-start one); runbook section 3.5 and the sbx-engine scripts should probe 'sbx daemon status' first and refuse to continue when it is not running; also 'schtasks /Run /TN' from Git Bash is rewritten as paths (MSYS), use PowerShell Start-ScheduledTask.
payload.evidence: daemon.log 2026-10-06T18:39:46: 'failed to create SDK client for runtime ... docker daemon is not reachable'; daemon pid 29100 started 18:36:30 by the background bash's 'sbx ls'; 'sbx diagnose' 9 passed 1 failed (Authentication: daemon unavailable) on that daemon

payload.description: Loop deficiency candidate 16 (found while planning the one-repository migration, ADR proposed AD-21): the supervisor holds one lock per checkout and the loop commits on a run branch in the mounted checkout, so once the plugin and the supervisor share «path» their two loops cannot run concurrently; one blocks on the other's lock for hours, and a run that switches branches under the other's working tree would corrupt it. The studio's project model also assumes a project root equals a checkout root (registry root, launch-epic ROOT, folder trust, hooks under CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR), which a nested root at apps/supervisor must be proven to satisfy. Fix to make: the supervisor launches each sandboxed run in its own git worktree of the checkout (worktree per run branch, removed at close-out, never following junctions), the lock becomes per worktree, and onboarding plus the drift check accept and verify nested project roots inside one repository; rehearse before the migration cut-over.

payload.description: Loop deficiency: Story 28.2's nearest-root rule excluded only the configured per-user store (TK_STUDIO_HOME) from being a project root, so with that variable set (every test, every supervisor worker) the default ~/.tk-studio/config.yaml still counted, and on Windows, where %TEMP% and every project under the profile sit below ~, «path» resolved as the project root for all of them: 17 failures and 2 errors in the lib suite and one conformance drive red on the host gate, while the Linux engine was green (/tmp is outside HOME). A real product bug on any Windows box, not only a test artifact. Closed by hand on loop/epic-28: a .tk-studio/ holding a store-only folder (registry/, measurements/, projects/) or matching the configured or default store root is a store, never a project; a test reproduces it on every OS. Hole to plug: the engine's Linux-only view keeps missing path-layout defects (holes 11/12/22 again); until the host-verify leg runs on every tk-studio run (Story 27.4 through the supervisor, 28.3/28.4), the hand-launch recipe must run tools/verify_host.py before any PR, and the planner should flag every rule that walks the filesystem upward as a Windows-profile case.

payload.description: Loop deficiency: the lib suite's test_restructure_rehearse module (34 tests, Story 28.1) was silently skipped in full on the Windows host because its PATH shim is built with os.symlink, which needs a privilege the box does not grant (WinError 1314); the host gate reported OK (skipped=34) and nothing flagged that the rehearsal script, written for this very host, had never run its tests here. Closed by hand on loop/epic-28: a fallback shim on symlink failure (each tool's own folder on PATH, a tool sharing a folder with bun or bmad-loop copied into the shim), plus three host-only fixture fixes (core.longpaths in the isolated gitconfig on Windows, shlex-quoted paths in a report assertion, an existing live file as a 'never written' probe). Hole to plug: the host gate should fail, or at least name, a test module whose every test skipped; verify_host.py can count skips per module and print them with the summary.

Closed by hand: see the fix PR. Hole to plug: `launch.py status` answers from the run files alone (the pure-data allowance: `.bmad-loop/runs/<id>/run.json` is host-visible through the worktrees mount) when bmad-loop is not on PATH, naming `bmad_loop: absent` and leaving liveness to the recorded engine pid (the hold and the /proc probe through sbx exec), or the supervisor runs the probe inside the run's sandbox for sbx-tier runs; and the conformance suite gains a drive of `status` on a host without bmad-loop.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 42): the supervisor's materialise runs `tk install` at the pin in every fresh worktree unconditionally (Story 27.1: "tk install at the pin, policy and routing copied, tk activate clean"), and on the-universe-awaits that install re-renders nine tracked files under _bmad/ (config.toml's module sections, core/bmb/bmad-loop config.yaml values such as user_name and project_name, module-help.csv, files-manifest.csv, and resolve_config.py / resolve_customization.py) even though the fresh worktree is already drift-clean ("8 components at pin, 1 base patch applied" from the checkout's drift_check.py before any install), so the launch's `bmad-loop validate` refused "git worktree is not clean — commit or stash before running" and the resubmitted run-epic-2 (q-run-epic-2-20261017T220515Z-f39af4, 2026-10-17 22:06Z) ended blocked after a $0.91 launch session; the close-out itself was clean (worktree removed, branch deleted, pin released: holes 34 and 38 hold). tk-studio's own tree is at the render, so its runs never saw it. Reproduced by hand in «path» (a worktree of TUA main): install_base.py reports normalized reverted 30, remaining 9. Hole to plug: materialise runs the drift check first and installs only on drift (a drift-clean fresh worktree needs no install; AD-19's lockstep is already satisfied), then copies the runtime and checks again; and the install's churn normalisation must not count a re-render of committed config values as a change to keep. Open for Tim: whether TUA's committed _bmad/ should be re-rendered by tk install (the render carries user_name Senpai, project_name "The Universe Awaits" and a gds primary_platform placeholder in place of TUA's committed answers), a TUA-side decision, not the studio's.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 43): a one-shot run-epic job whose launch ends blocked (the shipped run-epic type stops on_status [blocked]) is wedged: jobrun's evaluate_stop refuses every later submit while the job's last studio run is blocked ("stop: on_status — last run ended blocked"), `jobrun.py cancel` ends only resumable runs, and the supervisor's README names no operator verb: "the stop holds until a later run the studio actually ran reaches a terminal state", which no submit can start. Seen 2026-10-17 22:07Z on the-universe-awaits run-epic-2 after hole 42's blocked launch (the queue wrote `stopped {condition: on_status, state: blocked}`). A blocked launch is a normal, recoverable situation for a one-shot epic run (a dirty tree, a budget mismatch, a missing policy), not a reason to retire the job. Closed by hand: the blocked studio run's record moved aside out of ~/.tk-studio/projects/the-universe-awaits/runs/ so the job's last counted run is no longer blocked (its job-run event stays in the ledger). Hole to plug: a `jobrun.py clear-stop --job-id` verb (or `submit --clear-stop`) that records the operator's clearance as an event and lets the next run count, and the run-epic type's stop narrowed so a blocked launch that started no engine does not stop the job.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 45): on the agent PC the engine hold (`sbx exec <sb> tail --pid=<engine pid> -f /dev/null`, Story 27.2) spawned by a pacer pass dies with that pass (the tick and the drain are separate short-lived bun processes; the hold is not spawned detached from them), so every later pass finds the latest recorded hold dead and respawns one marked "supervisor restart": on TUA run q-run-epic-2-20261017T224219Z-39ae5a (2026-10-17) the events show a hold at 22:44:55 (the launch), one at 22:48:00 (the resume, spawned inside `serve` and still alive at 22:50, pid 54052) and then one per minute (22:48:03, 22:49:04, ...) while the alive hold is ignored because the check reads only the latest hold event. The engine is unaffected (the sandbox stays up while any exec is attached, and the VM pid is probed on each sweep), but the run's events gain a `hold` row per minute, each respawn costs an sbx exec, and a pass that holds nothing lets the sandbox stop between passes if no other exec is attached. Hole to plug: spawn the hold detached (its own process group / `detached: true`, stdio ignored) so it outlives the pass that spawned it; `respawnHolds` judges liveness over every recorded hold for the run, not the latest; and a respawn is recorded once per engine, not per pass.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 47): the engine's own verify on the-universe-awaits (policy [verify] commands = ["bash scripts/verify.sh"], run by bmad-loop after story 2-1's dev session landed c821251 at 2026-10-17 23:3xZ in run 20261017-224444-357a) failed rc=127 "scripts/verify.sh: line 25: dotnet: command not found" and the engine escalated ("verify environment fault: this is the run environment, not the story; fix the environment, then re-arm") and paused the run, discarding the pending graceful stop. The provisioning (tools/sbx-engine/provision-engine.sh, WITH_DOTNET=8.0) installs the SDK under ~/.dotnet and exports DOTNET_ROOT and the PATH only in ~/.profile, which only a login shell reads; the engine and its verify subprocesses run under the launch worker's bare `sbx exec` environment (PATH = the sandbox default plus ~/.local/bin), so dotnet is absent exactly where the loop needs it, while godot is already a ~/.local/bin link. Closed by hand: `ln -s ~/.dotnet/dotnet ~/.local/bin/dotnet` in the sandbox, then the run resumed (the re-arm resets the attempt budget). Hole to plug: provisioning links dotnet into ~/.local/bin (and any other toolchain it installs under HOME) and ends with a bare-exec check (`sbx exec <sb> dotnet --version`, `godot --version`) rather than a login-shell one; the supervisor's hold proves the sandbox but not its toolchain.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 46): the host verify leg (Story 27.4) runs a project's verify.host argv-only, never through a shell, with the supervisor's console environment, and on the agent PC a fresh console's PATH resolves a bare `bash` to the WindowsApps stub («path» the Store's App execution alias / WSL launcher; Git for Windows puts only Git\cmd on PATH, never its usr\bin), so TUA's `bash scripts/verify.sh` leg cannot run under Git Bash on the host as the project's config comment assumes (verified 2026-10-18 00:3xZ from the registry PATH; found while preparing the first close-out of run q-run-epic-2-20261017T224219Z-39ae5a). Closed in code: hostVerify puts Git's usr\bin first on the leg's PATH when a Git\cmd or Git\bin entry is on it and bash.exe exists there, and records the directory as `git_bash` on the host-verify event (apps/supervisor PR #132, hostverify.test.ts). Hole to plug: the runbook and the supervisor README name the stubs (done on PR #132's branch), and `tk-studio doctor` checks what a bare `bash` resolves to on the console PATH.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 48): the supervisor cuts run worktrees with `git worktree add --relative-paths` (Story 27.1: the engine microVM sees the gitdir through a different absolute path), which writes the repository extension `relativeworktrees` into the project's shared .git/config, and the .NET 8 SDK's source-control query (Microsoft.Build.Tasks.Git, run by every `dotnet build` of an SDK project) refuses it ("Error reading git repository information: Unsupported repository extension 'relativeworktrees'"), so every build of every checkout of the-universe-awaits failed, the main checkout included: the engine's verify of story 2-2 twice (run 20261017-234614-0cec, dev attempts 1 and 2, 2026-10-18 00:10Z and 00:29Z; the second dev session routed around it with an environment variable the engine's own verify never sees), the story deferred and the run paused "manual recovery needed", and the host verify leg would have failed the same way. Hole 47 masked it (story 2-1 never reached the build). Closed by hand on the run branch: EnableSourceControlManagerQueries=false in TUA's root Directory.Build.props (commit 1fb226a; nothing there uses SourceLink), proven by scripts/verify.sh green in the sandbox under bare exec and the build green on the host. Hole to plug: the runbook's git row and the supervisor README's Cut bullet name the extension and the property for .NET projects (done on PR #132's branch); the launch readiness check (or materialise) warns when a relative-path worktree holds a .NET solution without the property; TUA's props carry the fix to main through the run's PR (the-universe-awaits #4).

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 49): in the engine sandbox the .NET SDK lives under ~/.dotnet (provision-engine.sh WITH_DOTNET=8.0; hole 47 linked it into ~/.local/bin), but an apphost (every xunit v3 test project, so `dotnet test`, and any `dotnet run` output) finds the runtime only through DOTNET_ROOT or the registered install location («path» never through the dotnet on PATH, and the bare `sbx exec` environment the engine and its verify run under carries no DOTNET_ROOT (exported only in ~/.profile, which no shell reads there). TUA's test host printed "You must install .NET to run this application" (found by the second dev session of story 2-2, run 20261017-234614-0cec, 2026-10-18 00:2xZ, which exported DOTNET_ROOT by hand for its own run); the engine's verify would have failed at `dotnet test` as soon as the build passed. Closed by hand in claude-the-universe-awaits: `echo «path» | sudo tee «path» (the test host then runs, xUnit.net v3 on .NET 8.0.32; scripts/verify.sh green under bare exec, 1050 tests). Hole to plug: provisioning registers the install location and checks it (done on PR #132's branch), and the provisioning check runs an apphost rather than only `command -v dotnet`; the supervisor's hold proves the sandbox, not its toolchain.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 51): the supervisor's `bun test` hung twice on the box on 2026-10-18 (00:43Z and 00:50Z, branch fix/hole-46-host-verify-git-bash at 7148189 plus uncommitted docs) with no output at all, where the same suite passed earlier in the day (862/17/0 at about 20:30Z, 864/17/0 at 22:1xZ). Both times the e2e suite (test/command-line.test.ts) was inside a `bun src/cli.ts run studio-health --directory <temp fixture>` child that had no descendants (not waiting on a subprocess) and outlived the suite's 120 s spawn guard by more than ten minutes (a child alive 15 min; killed by hand with taskkill /T). The first run carried the box's real TK_SUPERVISOR_* environment (DB, WORK, BIND, TOKEN, TLS, SESSION_SECRET; the preload strips only the four notifier variables); the second had every TK_SUPERVISOR_* variable unset, so the environment is not the whole cause. Nothing in the suite bounds a hung child: bun's per-test timeout does not fire inside spawnSync, and a pipe into `tail` shows nothing until the end, so an operator sees only silence. Hole to plug: find why `run studio-health` does not return on this box in the e2e fixture (a TUA engine was live in the other sandbox both times; the fake CLAUDE_BIN is used, so not the host login), bound every e2e spawn with a kill on timeout, and make the preload strip every TK_SUPERVISOR_* variable rather than the notifier four; until then the gate for a supervisor commit runs the suites except the e2e one, and the e2e by hand.

The hostverify suite passed because it asserted the child's env, not what was spawned. Closed in code: a bare first token that Git's usr\bin holds is spawned by its full path there and the event records it as `resolved` (PR #132; the test now reads the capture wrapper's spec). The run's leg was re-run by hand on the host at the branch head (green) and PR #4 marked ready by hand. Hole to plug: an ended run's host leg should be re-runnable through a verb instead of a hand run plus a hand `gh pr ready`; a win32 test that spawns the real capture wrapper for a bare name.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 53): TUA's scripts/make-toy-world.sh wrote the regenerated manifest through Python's text mode, which uses the platform's line ending, so on the Windows host the file came back CRLF in an LF checkout (core.autocrlf false, `* text=auto`) and `git status --porcelain` named it modified: ToyWorldTests.Script_IsIdempotent failed on the host verify leg run by hand at the run branch head 4dfe60c (1 failed, 1057 passed, 2026-10-18 01:1xZ) while the engine's verify of the same commit in the Linux sandbox was green. The host leg and the engine's gate are different platforms, so a story the engine verified can still fail the host leg on platform-only defects, and nothing in the loop runs the host leg before the engine's commit counts as landed. Fixed on the run branch: newline="\n" in the write (the tree stays clean after two runs; ToyWorldTests green on the host). Hole to plug: the runbook names line endings and interpreter resolution among the host-leg differences for a .NET project; TUA's docs/loop-routing.md says the host leg is Windows.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 54): hole 46's fix edited `env.PATH` on a plain object copy of the supervisor's process.env, but a console-started process on Windows spells the key `Path`, and a plain copy is case-sensitive, so the edit added a second key `PATH` holding Git's usr\bin alone (the `?? ""` fallback) beside the real `Path`; the capture wrapper then resolved commands through a PATH of Git's usr\bin only. The EP-29 run q-run-epic-29-20261018T005721Z-5ecb17 ended `partial` at 2026-10-18 04:40Z with "host verify red: `uv run python tools/verify_host.py` failed to start: Executable not found in $PATH: \"uv\"" (35 ms, git_bash recorded) although its engine had finished all four stories on attempt 1, and PR #135 stayed a draft; the TUA run's exit-127 leg at 01:07Z (hole 52) ran under the same PATH. The hostverify suite passed because its env spelled the key PATH. Closed in code: the leg finds the key the environment uses (case-insensitive) and edits that one, never adding another (pathKey; PR #136; a test with a `Path` env asserts one key, prefixed). The EP-29 leg re-run by hand on the host at the branch head. Hole to plug: a win32 test that runs the real capture wrapper under a console-shaped env (`Path`), and an ended run's host leg re-runnable through a verb (hole 52's ask) so a red leg caused by the studio itself does not need a hand run plus a hand `gh pr ready`.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 55): the close-out opens a run's PR against main without merging or rebasing main into the run branch first, so a PR from a run that overlapped another merged story conflicts and GitHub refuses the merge. EP-29's PR #135 (branch cut from main 5cd5a8b at 00:58Z) conflicted at 06:07Z on 2026-10-18 with main after #131 (Story 28.6) merged: both stories bumped the driver contract (0.1.23 on main, 0.1.24 on the branch: the header line, the Story/rulings line), both added a version assertion and a test to test_driver_contract.py, and both appended a DW-27 entry to deferred-work.md. Resolved by hand in the side worktree with a script (both clauses in the header with 0.1.24 heading it; both tests, the 28.6 one checking its clause rather than the version; the run's deferral renumbered DW-28), gated by the contract suite, verify_host and the supervisor suites, then pushed. Hole to plug: the close-out merges main into the run branch before the PR opens (or after its engine ends), runs the host leg on the merged tree, and names a conflict it cannot resolve in the PR body and the ended reason; contract bumps by parallel stories need a merge rule in the contract's change policy (append the later clause after the earlier, the version the higher).

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 56): tk-studio's host verify leg (verify.host = uv run python tools/verify_host.py: the plugin's lib suite and conformance) never runs the supervisor's own suites, so a story in apps/supervisor is verified only by the engine's bun test on Linux in the sandbox, and Windows-only defects reach the PR unseen. EP-29's story 29-3 (the office projection) carried two: readJournal treated a directory in the journal's place as an empty file on Windows (a directory's size is 0 there, so nothing was read and no EISDIR fired), and two tests removed their fixture directory while the queue's SQLite file was still open (EBUSY on Windows, harmless on Linux); both found by hand on 2026-10-18 06:17Z running the suites per file on the merged branch (office.test.ts 40 pass, 3 fail), fixed by hand on the run branch before the merge. Hole to plug: the outer project's host leg runs the supervisor suites (per file, the e2e bounded, hole 51) when apps/supervisor changed, or the nested project's own verify.host is honoured for a run whose commits touch it; until then every supervisor PR gets the per-file suite run on the host by hand.
payload.evidence: scratchpad buntest-ep29-merge.log; apps/supervisor src/office.ts readJournal and test/office.test.ts on supervisor/run-q-run-epic-29-20261018T005721Z-5ecb17

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 57): the installed launcher's self-update (tk-studio update, the cli slot) hands the uv tool install to a detached cli-update.cmd that waits only for the launcher process that spawned it (tasklist on that one PID) and then runs uv tool install --force on the new wheel; a second launcher process started meanwhile (tk-studio doctor right after the update, 2026-10-18 21:43Z on TIM-PC-2) still held Scripts\tk-studio.exe, uv failed with 'failed to remove directory ...\tk-studio-cli\Scripts: Access is denied (os error 5)' after it had already removed Lib, and the launcher was left broken (ImportError: cannot import name plugin_leg; doctor printing nothing), with no retry, no rollback to the previous wheel and no notice beyond cli-update.log. Closed by hand: the same uv tool install re-run from the session into the real tree (tk-studio-cli 0.1.2, doctor 16 pass), the leftover cli-update.cmd/.log removed (the doctor's cli-update-helper row names them). Hole to plug: the helper waits until no process holds the tool environment (or retries the install on EACCES with a bound), verifies the new launcher answers (tk-studio doctor --json) and reinstalls the previous wheel when it does not, and the launcher refuses to start a second self-update while one is pending.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 58): POST /runs/{id}/cancel on an sbx-tier run asks the engine to stop through launch.py on the HOST, where bmad-loop is absent by design (hole 38 fixed the probe and the sweep but not the cancel's engine_stop), so every cancel of an sbx run records engine_stop ok=false 'launch stop refused: bmad-loop is not on PATH' and falls through to the in-VM kill (which found the paused engine not running: run q-run-epic-24-20261019T171606Z-dace1f, 2026-10-19 17:47Z). Harmless for a paused run; a live sbx engine would be killed rather than stopped. Hole to plug: the cancel's engine_stop runs launch.py stop inside the run's sandbox (vmLaunchStatus's sibling) for an sbx run. Also seen: a paused run's queued graceful stop is discarded by the pause (as before), so a ruling that relaunches starts the next story at once; with 24-3's paired runs too expensive for the day's quota, the operator cancelled the run and closed the story out by hand (ruling in the spec, the host leg by hand, the PR merged).
payload.evidence: run q-run-epic-24-20261019T171606Z-dace1f ended cancelled 17:47:37Z; apps/supervisor src/cli.ts cancelRun engine_stop

payload.description: Hole 58 follow-up: the cancel of the paused sbx run q-run-epic-24-20261019T171606Z-dace1f (17:47Z) recorded no pin-released event and left claude-tk-studio running after the run ended cancelled, so the cancel path on a paused run also skips the pin release every other end path asks for (Story 27.2); harmless when the next run pins the same sandbox, a leak otherwise.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 60): the runbook's recipe for a new secret, setx then restart the supervisor tab, does not deliver the variable: a tab restarted inside an already-running Windows Terminal inherits the terminal process's environment, which predates the setx, so the restarted supervisor (10:37 local, 2026-10-24) had no TK_ATLASSIAN_* and its sbx worker passed nothing through (PR #159's pass-through emits -e NAME only for variables present); the first run-epic-31 run (q-run-epic-31-20261024T153925Z-9d7c40) launched story 31.1 with an engine whose /proc/<pid>/environ held none of the names and was cancelled before the dev session could fail on it (bootstrap 6.74 USD spent). Hole to plug: the supervisor reads the pass-through variables from the User environment (HKCU\Environment) at each worker spawn when its own environment lacks them, so a setx is enough and no restart is needed for a new or rotated secret; the runbook says Windows Terminal, not the tab, must restart for anything else.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 66): the supervisor process disappeared at about 16:20Z on 2026-10-25 while run q-run-epic-32-20261025T153557Z-06109b (story 32.7) was live (its queue.db-wal was last written 16:20Z; the API refused connections from 16:1xZ; no bun process). The engine kept running in the sandbox and the run waits for the supervisor's sweep after a restart, so nothing is lost, but the cause is unknowable: the supervisor writes no log file on disk (the Windows Terminal tab's console is its only log) and a restart wipes the console. Fix to make: the supervisor logs to a rotating file under «path» (or the host ledger) with its start, stop and every uncaught error, and doctor reports the last stop reason; the runbook names the file.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 67): Windows Smart App Control switched itself from evaluation to enforced on TIM-PC-2 at 2026-10-25 08:03Z (CI policy VerifiedAndReputablePolicyState=1; first Code Integrity 3077 block 03:03 local). Since then user-mode Code Integrity blocks every unsigned, reputation-less executable: bun's node_modules\.bin\*.exe shims (so the host leg's studio-web gate, bun run verify -> vite build, dies with 'bun: unknown error' in one second: story 32.7's run ended partial, draft PR #181, though the branch builds and its 177 vitest tests pass through bun's own runtime), uv's tool launcher %LOCALAPPDATA%\tk-studio\bin\tk-studio.exe ('An Application Control policy has blocked this file'), and any future unsigned binary (pip/uv console-script launchers, bun-made shims). The engine in the Linux sandbox is unaffected. Fix to make: (1) the studio-web scripts run tools through bun's runtime, never a .bin shim (build: bun x vite build; test: bun x vitest run), and doctor warns when SAC is enforced; (2) Tim decides on SAC itself (Windows Security > App & browser control > Smart App Control > Off; irreversible without a reinstall) or signs/allow-lists the shims.

Kept as hardening: apps/studio-web's scripts run vite and vitest through bun's runtime (bun x), so the host leg's web gate no longer depends on an unsigned launcher. Still to make: doctor warns when SAC or a CI policy is enforced; the runbook names SAC under first-boot steps (turn it off before the evaluation period ends, or it self-enforces).

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 68): an sbx exec from a Claude session on a stopped engine sandbox starts it without the Max login (the sandbox then reports claude auth status loggedIn=false, authMethod none), and the supervisor's pin (sbx run -d --name) is a no-op on a running sandbox, so the drain's in-sandbox login preflight fails on every pass and the queued run never claims; the refusal is printed to the console only (no queue event, no notification): run q-run-epic-32-20261026T133057Z-0d6e7c sat queued from 13:31Z on 2026-10-26 until the console was read through computer use. Remedy: stop the sandbox so the next pin starts it with the login. Fix to make: the pin restarts a running sandbox whose login probe fails (or the preflight failure is recorded as a queue event and notified), and sessions never exec a stopped sandbox (check sbx ls first).
payload.evidence: supervisor console: drain summary state blocked, reason 'harness auth: Max login missing or expired (claude auth status exited 1)'; sbx exec claude-tk-studio claude auth status --json -> loggedIn false at 14:1xZ

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 69): the engine sandbox's Max login is the global anthropic sbx secret (an OAuth grant stored by sbx secret set anthropic --oauth at provisioning on 2026-10-15); its refresh token expired at 2026-10-25T23:38Z (the sandbox's placeholder ~/.claude/.credentials.json shows empty tokens and refreshTokenExpiresAt 1792971511452), after which every sandbox start gets SBX_CRED_ANTHROPIC_MODE=none, claude auth status reports loggedIn false, and the supervisor's in-sandbox preflight blocks every claim with 'Max login missing or expired' printed to the console only. Nothing warned beforehand and the first sign was a run sitting queued (q-run-epic-32-20261026T133057Z-0d6e7c). Renewal is the owner's sign-in: sbx secret set anthropic --oauth on the host, then a sandbox restart. Fix to make: doctor and the activate drift check read refreshTokenExpiresAt through sbx exec and warn a week ahead; the supervisor's preflight failure becomes a queue event with a notifier line; the runbook names the renewal command and the ~10-day lifetime.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 73): a cancelled run's close-out opened a PR that nothing closes. Queue run q-run-epic-31-20261024T153925Z-9d7c40 was cancelled on operator request at 2026-10-24T15:55Z (hole 60), yet the supervisor opened PR #161 for its branch at 16:41Z and the PR sat open, conflicting, for three days while the relaunch landed the same spec through #162 and Epic 31 completed with #162 to #168. payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 75): the first real use of POST /runs/{id}/verify (Story 33.8) failed with VerifyFailed: worktree activate drift: result 'drift'. The verb cuts a fresh worktree and materialises it the way a run does, and materialise gates on the activation drift check being clean; since Story 33.2 the drift check has a sixth plane, sandbox-login, which reports 'missing' whenever the project's sandbox is stopped (it is released after every run and the verify verb never pins it), so the check can never be clean for a verify, and tk install inside the worktree changes nothing. The run path never saw it because the pin starts the sandbox before materialise. Fix to make: materialise judges only the planes it owns (bmad-base, plugin, store, vault) and reports the sandbox-login plane without failing on it (the pin owns the login, 33.3); and the drift check should report a stopped sandbox as not-checked rather than missing, as doctor already does (skipped). Until then a red host leg is re-run by hand (the runbook recipe).

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 76): a conformance drive green in the engine's sandbox and red on the host because its bound has no Windows headroom. Story 34.1's drive contracts/conformance/e2e_engine_gate.py runs the whole bun test test/hostverify.test.ts (33 cases, 43 s on the agent PC with real git worktrees) under BOUND_S = 50 s, itself forced under the runner's 60 s per-drive timeout; inside the drive the suite passes 50 s on Windows and the drive reports 'hung past 50s' (surfaces.tk-studio-launch headless-clean), so the hand gate on the 34.1 branch tip failed conformance although the lib suite and all 34 supervisor suites were green. Fix to make: a drive runs only the cases it owns (bun test -t with the story's test names), never a whole suite; a drive's bound is derived from the host-measured suite time with headroom, and the runner's per-drive timeout is a documented knob.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 77): a bash verify.host can never be green under the supervisor's host leg on Windows. The leg's capture wrapper (hostverify.ts CAPTURE) opens the command's stdout and stderr files in append mode (fs.openSync(file, 'a')) and hands the handles to the child; MSYS bash cannot write to an append-only handle ('echo: write error: Bad file descriptor'), so every echo and printf in the script fails while the .NET children write fine, the script's own lines vanish from the capture, and its exit status follows its last command, verify.sh's closing echo 'verify: OK', which fails: exit 1. The Universe Awaits' host leg was red on every run since 2026-10-18 (hole 50 was blamed then) and 34.1's engine step never ran (skipped: verify.host red). Fix to make: the wrapper opens fresh files in write mode ('w'); a host-leg test runs a bash step with echoes on Windows and asserts its lines and exit 0; the hole-52 rule (bash spawned by its full usr/bin path) stays.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 78): the host leg's engine gate hangs when the project calls a bare godot. Story 34.1's leg prepends the folder of GODOT to the step's PATH, but that folder holds Godot_v4.7.2-stable_mono_win64_console.exe and no file named godot, so a project's bare godot (The Universe Awaits' scripts/engine-gate.sh) resolves further down PATH to WinGet's link «path» Files\WinGet\Links\godot.exe, the GUI build; under the leg (hidden window, no console) its --headless --import --quit never returned (45 minutes, killed by the operator). The host step was green by then (the first green TUA host verify ever, after hole 77), so the engine step is what kept the proof red. Fix to make: a project's engine gate calls the engine through GODOT when set (TUA: GODOT_BIN=${GODOT:-godot}, cygpath for the Windows path), as the contract's verify.engine section and 34.1's acceptance record already assume; and the leg should also expose the console exe as godot (a per-run shim folder first on PATH with a godot.exe hardlink), so a bare godot never reaches the GUI build; the engine step needs its own guard shorter than the leg's.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 80): the host leg and Story 34.1's conformance drive assume apps/supervisor/node_modules exists, and a fresh worktree has none. Every verify worktree (33.8) and every run whose dev session never ran bun install (a story that does not touch the supervisor, such as 34.2) runs the e2e_engine_gate drive's bun test without the supervisor's dependencies ('Cannot find package js-yaml'), so conformance goes red and so does the lib suite through test_conformance's real-plugin case; the host leg's own supervisor gate (33.4) then fails the same way plus tsc ('Cannot find type definition file for bun'). Story 34.2's run went partial on its own worktree for this reason, and its re-verify failed on all three gates. Fix to make: the host gate installs the supervisor's dependencies (bun install --frozen-lockfile, bounded, logged) when node_modules is missing or older than the lockfile, before the per-file suites and tsc; the drive does the same within its bound (or reports not_run naming the missing install when it cannot); materialise could install for every fresh worktree of a project that declares a bun app.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 81): a story that introduces a contract schema and carries open SPEC questions reaches its dev session with no plan, and the session can only halt. Epic 34's launch bootstrap wrote plans/34-1.md only; the gates wrote the next stories' plans as they went (34-2 to 34-5), but 34.5's relaunch moved straight to 34.6, whose SPEC open questions CAP-11/CAP-12 had no design note and no plans/34-6.md, so the dev session escalated an intent gap with six questions (the colour map, the art path, the value sets, the derived file, .glb or .gltf, the deterministic label) and paused the run. Fix to make: the bootstrap writes a plan for every story of the epic (or the gate always writes the next story's plan before the loop moves on), and the launch refuses to dispatch a story whose SPEC open questions have no settled design note; the operator wrote plans/34-6.md by hand this time.

payload.description: Loop deficiency (hole 82): the host leg runs the supervisor's bun suites with the box's TK_STUDIO_ROOT (the served checkout on main), so a story that changes the plugin lib or a contract and tests the supervisor against the change goes red on the host leg: 34.5's editor_in_the_loop definition flag was refused by main's job.py ('unknown field(s)'). Fix made: verify_host.py's supervisor_env sets TK_STUDIO_ROOT to the repo under verification. Beside it, two Windows-only test defects the sandbox engine never sees (the supervisor suite runs on the host only): a Windows temp path in a bare double-quoted YAML scalar (expected hexadecimal character) and shutil.which answering blender.EXE for a fake named blender.
